title: Master Guide to Confusing German Grammar Usage (A vs B)

a0_a2.point: sie (she) vs sie (they) vs Sie (formal you)
a0_a2.core_difference: Capitalization and verb conjugation distinguish singular 'she', plural 'they', and formal 'you'.
a0_a2.usage_a: sie (she) takes 3rd person singular verb ending (-t, e.g. sie wohnt).
a0_a2.usage_b: sie (they) takes plural verb ending (-en, e.g. sie wohnen). Formal 'Sie' is always capitalized and takes plural verb ending (-en).
examples: Sie wohnt in Berlin. (She lives in Berlin)
Sie wohnen in Berlin. (They live in Berlin)
Woher kommen Sie? (Where are you from? - formal)
a0_a2.quick_logic: Check verb ending (-t vs -en) and capital letter S.
common_mistakes: ❌ Sie wohnt hier (meaning 'They live here') → ✓ Sie wohnen hier.
a0_a2.memory_trick: Capital S = Formal Respect. Lowercase s + -t = She. Lowercase s + -en = They.

a0_a2.core_difference: Use 'kein' to negate nouns with indefinite articles or no articles; use 'nicht' to negate verbs, adjectives, proper nouns, or definite nouns.
a0_a2.usage_a: kein declines like 'ein' and negates countable/uncountable nouns without definite articles.
a0_a2.usage_b: nicht negates verbs, adjectives, adverbs, possessives, and sentences.
a0_a2.quick_logic: Negating a noun preceded by ein/eine or no article? → KEIN. Otherwise → NICHT.
common_mistakes: ❌ Ich habe nicht Geld. → ✓ Ich habe kein Geld.
a0_a2.memory_trick: Kein = No + Noun. Nicht = Not + Everything else.

a0_a2.core_difference: Both mean 'because', but 'weil' sends the conjugated verb to the end of the clause, whereas 'denn' keeps standard word order (Position 0).
a0_a2.usage_a: weil is a subordinating conjunction (Verb at the end).
a0_a2.usage_b: denn is a coordinating conjunction in Position 0 (Subject + Verb follow directly).
examples: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn ich bin krank.
a0_a2.quick_logic: weil = verb kicked to the end. denn = normal sentence order.
common_mistakes: ❌ ...weil ich bin krank. → ✓ ...weil ich krank bin.
a0_a2.memory_trick: Weil kicks the verb to the end!

b1_b2.core_difference: Use 'als' for single past events or past time periods. Use 'wenn' for repeated past actions, present events, or future events.
b1_b2.usage_a: als for one single finished event or phase in the past (e.g. when I was a child, when I arrived yesterday).
b1_b2.usage_b: wenn for repeated events ('whenever') or present/future conditions.
examples: Als ich ein Kind war, wohnte ich in Hamburg.
Jedes Mal, wenn er kam, brachten wir Kuchen.
Wenn es morgen regnet, bleiben wir drinnen.
b1_b2.quick_logic: Single past moment = ALS. Repeated or present/future = WENN.
common_mistakes: ❌ Wenn ich 10 Jahre alt war... → ✓ Als ich 10 Jahre alt war...
b1_b2.memory_trick: ALS = A Lone Story in the past. WENN = Whenever / Future.
